overview: The CC Energy & Environment Committee serves as an advisory body for Medford's sustainability programs, climate policy, and environmental health initiatives. Spanning meetings from early 2024 through late 2026, the committee has provided oversight for municipal decarbonization, waste reduction strategies, and urban forestry management. Key efforts include the rollout of the 'Electrify Medford' heat pump coaching program and the annual coordination of the Harvest Your Energy Festival. At the most recent meetings, the committee has focused on tracking the city's Climate Action and Adaptation Plan and advocating for local restrictions on anticoagulant rodenticides.

threads.name: Municipal Decarbonization and Electrification
threads.summary: The committee monitors progress on citywide energy initiatives, including the 'Electrify Medford' program which provides residential heat pump coaching. Early updates tracked recruitment for coaching roles and municipal aggregation bidding that increased renewable energy content. Work expanded to include school HVAC upgrades, solar installations at the Andrews and McGlynn schools, and the transition of the municipal fleet to electric vehicles. Recent reports highlight a steady downward trend in building and stationary energy emissions as the city pursues Climate Leader certification.

threads.name: Waste Reduction and Composting
threads.summary: This thread covers the city's transition toward zero-waste goals, beginning with the rollout of citywide curbside composting. The committee investigated a ban on black plastic takeout containers and researched specialty recycling options for materials like plastic film. In 2026, members engaged in an extensive debate regarding a proposed 18-month rollout for bi-weekly trash collection. Ongoing work involves a dedicated zero-waste working group and community outreach on waste diversion.

threads.name: Urban Forestry and Tree Preservation
threads.summary: The committee collaborates with Trees Medford to expand the city's tree canopy and manage reforestation efforts. Initial work focused on drafting tree ordinances and addressing concerns regarding municipal enforcement and mitigation fees. The body also supported park tree inventories, residential shade tree distributions, and the mapping of significant 'landmark' trees. By mid-2026, the City Council moved forward with a public tree ordinance following committee advocacy and the development of local reforestation bills.

threads.name: Climate Action and Adaptation Plan (CAAP) Tracking
threads.summary: In late 2025, the committee began a systematic review of the city's progress across approximately 150 strategies outlined in the Climate Action Plan. Members utilized spreadsheets to monitor individual sections and established a process for five-year reviews. Recent meetings involved conducting gap analyses to identify which climate action points require further attention. This work is intended to ensure accountability for long-term sustainability goals.

threads.name: Legislative Advocacy and Public Health
threads.summary: The committee frequently evaluates state and local legislation, including endorsing the Climate Change Superfund bill and reviewing siting reforms for clean energy. Members have hosted educational presentations on environmental hazards such as PFAS, neurotoxins, and light pollution. Recent efforts have centered on banning anticoagulant rodenticides to protect local wildlife, culminating in presentations from ecological experts. The body also researches model ordinances for dark sky lighting and data center regulations.

threads.name: Harvest Your Energy Festival
threads.summary: The committee is responsible for the planning and execution of this annual community event held at the McGlynn Middle School. Activities include coordinating volunteer shifts, managing an electric vehicle showcase, and organizing electronics recycling and shredding services. Each year, the body reviews logistics such as shuttle bus services and vendor recruitment. Planning for the festival typically begins in early spring and concludes with a debriefing in the late fall.

threads.name: Climate Resilience and Land Use
threads.summary: Resilience work has focused on infrastructure upgrades to mitigate flooding and extreme heat. The committee reviewed a 'green score' zoning overhaul designed to encourage permeable surfaces and green roofs for large developments in flood zones. Other projects include the development of the Willis Avenue Community Center as a resilience hub and monitoring sea level rise at the Amelia Earhart Dam. The body continues to track hazard mitigation planning and the environmental impact of proposed recreational additions to local ponds.
